clue.text: Recital isn't ruined with tense musician

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A performance falls apart because a nervous player was on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges RECITALISNT; T is added after. 'tense' looks like an adjective for the musician but is the grammar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinettist is a player of the clarinet, so is one kind of musician.

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: Pull back a dog that is chasing another dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The two uses of 'dog' differ: first the animal, then the verb meaning to follow closely. In a down clue 'on' puts one piece above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail something is to restrict or cut it short, as a rein checks a horse.

clue.text: Saw a cross on small island

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
IOM abbreviates the Isle of Man, a small island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Someone saw an X marked on a little island, like a treasure map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see but is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, as is an axiom, a self-evident principle.

indicators.note: revolting suggests turning over, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mad ruler is in power and the people are rising against them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' rearranges NUTREIGNS.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel fighting against established authority.

clue.text: Periodically need farm to produce cheese

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A dairy farm occasionally has to make cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' takes the even letters of 'need farm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese, an example of the category.

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a treat is an indulgence
sure is a casual way of saying of course

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an endless indulgence is allowed, and a lover says yes, darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts TREAT to TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure is a much-loved person, used as an endearment like darling.

clue.text: Trade involving launch of vanishing cream

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the trade word wraps around the letter

parts.note: a sale is an act of trade

indicators.note: a launch is a start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A cosmetics firm launches a vanishing cream on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts V inside SALE. Vanishing cream is a real cosmetic, which hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is a soothing ointment, a kind of cream applied to the skin.

clue.text: One drives over hill in fog

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the fog word

parts.note: mist is light fog
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone drives across a hill shrouded in fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OTOR inside MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is a person who drives a car, so is one who drives.

parts.note: par is the usual or normal level
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: An ordinary chap offers a justification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excuse' is the verb, forgive, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon someone is to excuse or forgive their offence.

parts.note: reins are the controls of a horse
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A politician restores controls in the face of European junk.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to put back into a former position, i.e. restore.

clue.text: Sponge from a sucker taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback read as taken backwards, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: a sucker is a fool, someone easily duped

explanation.surface: A dupe is startled to be relieved of his sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns AFOOL round.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah, also spelt loofa, is a fibrous gourd used as a bath sponge.

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the other letters

parts.note: a mire is a muddy mess

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician earns respect despite a political mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D between A and MIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to regard them highly, i.e. respect them.

parts.note: a steroid is a type of drug

explanation.surface: A drug is turning into crack, slang rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example: an asteroid is a rock in space.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun, one example of a rock.

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
fed means nourished

explanation.surface: A well-fed meadow sprouts fresh plants.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is a loose, playful one.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafed describes a plant that has put out leaves, its fresh growth.

clue.text: Sweetheart consumed by every bloody story

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed by, so the letter goes inside the others

parts.note: all means every one
gory means bloody
the heart of sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A lover is eaten up in a violent tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweetheart gives E, the middle letter of sweet, a standard crossword device. 'consumed by' puts it inside ALLGORY.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story with a hidden symbolic meaning.

clue.text: Part of Republican inside rebellious group

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation within the group word

parts.note: a faction is a dissenting group within a party

explanation.surface: Part of the Republican party is a rebel splinter group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts R within FACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction is a small part or portion of a whole.

clue.text: Personality of a Conservative in authority

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the authority word

parts.note: a charter is a document granting authority or rights

explanation.surface: A Tory in power has a strong personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AC inside CHARTER, splitting it as CHAR-AC-TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Character means a person's distinctive nature or personality.

clue.text: Bishop close accepting first female minister

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the woman goes inside the other letters

parts.note: RR abbreviates Right Rev., the formal style of a bishop
Eve is the first woman in the Bible
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A bishop nearly takes in the first female minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'close' as nearly, but it is the noun meaning end. The bishop's abbreviation comes from his formal style, Right Rev.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverend is a member of the clergy, a minister of religion.

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds when a race begins
the latter is the last of two, the final one

explanation.surface: Spread betting on the odds ahead of a final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread betting' is a real phrase, which hides that 'Spread' alone is the definition. 'before' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter is to splash or scatter something widely, spreading it about.

parts.note: to set is to place
a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball

explanation.surface: Somewhere to sit that has a back to lean on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a settee is a seat with a supporting back.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, a seat that supports the sitter's back.

clue.text: Extracted from gum, a sticky substance

indicators.note: extracted from means drawn out of, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: A sticky substance is taken from a gum.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites 'a sticky substance' as the definition, but 'sticky' is part of the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin used as a sealant or adhesive, a particular substance.

clue.text: Admit criminal with iron shackles, gutted

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: gutted means with the insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A criminal owns up while in iron shackles, devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like 'heartbroken' but keeps only the ends of shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess is to admit guilt or wrongdoing.

indicators.note: conceding a goal is letting it in, so the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: a tether is a lead or rope for an animal
OG is the football abbreviation for own goal

explanation.surface: Manchester United throws away a lead by scoring an own goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture hides that 'United' is the definition and 'lead' a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Together means joined or united as one.

clue.text: Subject of article on Middle East

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A news piece on the Middle East is the topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a discussion or work.

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the retreat word goes after the conflict word

parts.note: war is armed conflict
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A sentry falls back after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden is a keeper or guardian, someone who guards a place or people.

definitions.meaning: the past of drive, to control a vehicle
a large moving crowd, of animals or people

explanation.surface: Someone kept a crowd in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Drove is both the past tense of drive, to steer, and a noun for a herd or throng.

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken, so the letters entered match how the ring word is pronounced

parts.note: a bow is a knot tied in a loop, a ring of ribbon

explanation.surface: Offering a ring to one's beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a sound-alike: BEAU is said like bow, the looped knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer, a sweetheart.

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the entry sounds like the synonym

parts.note: eerie means unearthly or spooky

explanation.surface: A rumoured otherworldly nest of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, high on a crag.

parts.note: elect means chosen or picked
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: An orchestra conductor selects the right song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' points to music but means an electrical conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode conducts electricity into or out of a medium, so is an electrical conductor.

clue.text: Request a hard ground for base

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking for firm earth to build a foundation on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun for earth but is the past participle of grind, the anagram signal for REQUESTAHARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Headquarters is an organisation's base, its central place of operations.
